releaseEvidence: The official v8.23.0 GitHub release says the media editor was completely redesigned for tablets, foldables, and screens of all sizes.
The same official release says the editor can remove a video's audio track before sending.
Official commits d6b0826f, ee59bb40, 1fd343df, a4793ebb, and 24fffdf2 connect the editor state refactor, audio-removal pipeline, discard confirmation, and user feedback.

implementationEvidence.testEvidenceNote: Focused tests cover state derivation, event handoff, media-save failure states, mute-control eligibility, transform serialization compatibility, and the transcoder's expanded audio-removal input.

baseFailureEvidence: The v8.22.2 tree has no MediaEditState or MediaEditViewModel production files and no corresponding focused tests.
The v8.22.2 tree has no ToggleVideoMuted event, no isMuteVideoAudioEnabled state, and no persisted videoMuted transform field.
The v8.22.2 transcoder has no mute-audio input and therefore cannot force audio-track omission from edited output.
The v8.23.0 tree contains all of those state, persistence, UI, and transcoding surfaces.

boundaryAudit.verification: Local read-only git object queries and the official GitHub compare endpoint agree on ancestry and containment.

longHorizonSignals: The task crosses responsive UI, saved flow state, per-item editor state, pre-upload invalidation, attachment serialization, and video transcoding.
The state graph includes focus and reorder transitions, mute and unmute transitions, edited-media send preparation, and confirmed versus canceled discard.
Compatibility must be preserved for existing serialized transforms that lack the new field.
